tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company received order dated January 28, 2025 from Joint Commissioner, Central Goods & Services Tax on February 04, 2025 demanding penalty under Section 74 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 read with relevant provisions of the State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 amounting to Rs. 61,15,042/-. The appeal was filed by the Company and pending before Honourable Appellate Authority, Commissioner (Appeals), Central GST against the demand of penalty amounting to Rs. 61,15,042.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Joint Commissioner, Central Goods & Services Tax, Ahmedabad
tax_litigation.status: The hearing in respect of the appeal pending before the Hon’ble Appellate Authority, Commissioner (Appeals), Central GST, against the penalty demand of Rs. 61,15,042 was held in December 2025. The Appellate Authority has reserved the order, and the final outcome is awaited from the authority.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company received order dated January 28, 2025 from Joint Commissioner, Central Goods & Services Tax on February 04, 2025 demanding penalty under Section 74 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 read with relevant provisions of the State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 amounting to Rs. 61,15,042/-. The Company has already paid the amount of GST under reverse charge basis and the same has been appropriated by the Authority in its order. tax_litigation.status: Hearing in respect of the said appeal was held in December 2025, and the appellate authority, vide its order dated 16.01.2026, has allowed the appeal in favour of the Company by quashing the demand of Rs. 61,15,042.

operating_notes.text: Total volume in FY26 reached 223.67 mmscm, driven by CNG volume growth.
CNG remains the largest contributor to volume, accounting for 61% of total operational revenue in FY26.
Capex for CGD network in Namakkal and Tiruchirappalli experienced delays due to site identification issues and routine government permissions for pipeline laying.

timeline.summary: Dr. Rajiv I. Modi, Cadila Pharmaceuticals Limited, and IRM Trust declared no encumbrance on IRM Energy shares for FY2025-26 under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4).
IRM Energy Limited scheduled a virtual earnings conference call for May 9, 2026, at 3:00 PM (IST) to discuss Q4 & FY2026 updates, attended by senior management.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹304 Cr (+5.2% YoY), net profit ₹12.75 Cr (+190.4% YoY).
IRM Energy presented its Q4FY26 and FY26 investor presentation highlighting a 73% YoY jump in Q4 consolidated EBITDA.
IRM Energy Limited’s **Akshit Nandkishor Soni** shared the earnings conference call recording (May 09, 2026, 3:00 PM IST) for Q4FY26 via the company website.
On May 9, 2026, IRM Energy held its Q4FY26 earnings conference call, highlighting a 9% YoY volume growth and outlining expansion plans for FY27.
IRM Energy disclosed its Q4FY26 monitoring agency report showing ₹112.97 Cr capex utilization for CGD network development against a scheduled ₹236.38 Cr due to implementation delays.
IRM Energy Limited’s **Akshit Soni** and **Nandkishor Soni** scheduled a virtual Investors/Analysts Meeting on **May 21, 2026, 5:00–6:00 PM (IST)** at Centrum Nakshatra III.
IRM Energy Limited scheduled an Analyst/Investor Earnings Conference Call on Monday, November 02, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. (IST).
